Where it began

Umesh Yadav was born in Nagpur on 25 October 1987. He came to proper cricket late. Until 2007 he had only played with a tennis ball, and his college side turned him away because he had no club. So he found one, joining Vidarbha Gymkhana and bowling with a leather ball for the first time in the local league.

Things moved quickly after that. The Vidarbha captain, Pritam Gandhe, saw how fast he was and helped him on his way. His first first-class match, against Madhya Pradesh, came in November 2008, and he finished that first Ranji Trophy season with 20 wickets from four matches.

The player

His first one-day international came against Zimbabwe in May 2010, and his Test debut followed in November 2011 against the West Indies. That made him the first Vidarbha cricketer to play Test cricket. He took two wickets in the second innings as India won by five wickets.

Within weeks he was in Australia, where he played all four Tests and took his first five-wicket haul, at Perth. Between 2011 and 2023 he played 57 Tests and took 170 wickets at 30.96, with a best of 6 for 88. He was part of the side that won the 2013 Champions Trophy, and at the 2015 World Cup no Indian bowler took more wickets than his 18.

What made him special

Pace, first and last. He was among the fastest bowlers India has produced, touching 152.5 km/h, and he liked to attack the stumps rather than wait for an edge. That made him a real force for India at home. His spell at Dharamshala against Australia in 2017, when he removed both openers on the third day, helped seal victory there.

Like many fast men, he could leak the odd run when the radar wandered. It was the price of pace, and 170 Test wickets suggest it was worth paying. At home in Vidarbha he kept giving: in January 2019 his 12 for 79 against Kerala in the Ranji Trophy semi-final carried his side into the final.

Away from the middle

He was a familiar face in the Indian Premier League, playing for Delhi, Kolkata Knight Riders and Royal Challengers Bangalore among others. In 2012 he took 19 wickets for Delhi, the fourth-highest haul of that season.

And finally

Fast bowlers are not usually remembered for their batting, and his 460 Test runs came at 11.22. But in October 2019 against South Africa he hit 31 runs from just 10 balls, a strike rate of 310, which was a Test record for an innings at the time. As far as anyone knows, he made no apology to the bowlers.
